title: Tech Edition
dek: Linux gaming is reverse-engineering the Xbox PC stack, GoldenEye is escaping the N64 through readable source, and agent oversight is becoming an interface-design problem rather than a checkbox.

lead_stories.headline: Xodus is reverse-engineering the Xbox PC stack instead of waiting for Game Pass to support Linux
lead_stories.summary: Xodus can already authenticate with Xbox services, obtain game licenses, download MSIXVC packages and decrypt executables on demand. The remaining hard problem is runtime compatibility: reproducing enough Xbox Gaming Runtime behavior in Wine and related components for games to start correctly.
lead_stories.why_it_matters: This is not another launcher skin. It targets proprietary identity, licensing, packaging and runtime services that Proton alone does not provide.

reader.standfirst: The obstacle to PC Game Pass on Linux is increasingly the service stack around a game, not simply DirectX.
body: Wine and Proton translate Windows and graphics APIs, but GDK titles can also depend on Xbox authentication, entitlements, encrypted MSIXVC packages and the Xbox Gaming Runtime.
Xodus splits those concerns into Rust crates and a service process. Its README reports working login, authorization, package download, license acquisition and on-demand executable decryption.
The repo is actively moving: an August 27 commit added an XStore license-token API; earlier commits added tests and a binary parser.
The README is also explicit that Wine-side Xbox-service compatibility and MSIXVC2 support remain unfinished.
reader.context: The project is being developed by contributors around Heroic Games Launcher and related reverse-engineering work.
key_points: Identity and licensing are already partly working.
Runtime-service emulation is the larger remaining boundary.
The service process is intended as the integration point for clients and games.
reader.limitations: It is not yet a consumer-ready way to play the Game Pass catalog on Linux.
reader.what_to_try: Inspect xodus-service after reading the workspace layout to see how volatile external services are isolated behind one local boundary.

lead_stories.headline: GoldenEye's completed decompilation is already turning into a native cross-platform game
lead_stories.summary: Goldeneye-Native compiles reconstructed GoldenEye 007 C directly for Windows, macOS and Linux, replacing N64 hardware interfaces with modern platform code. It already adds modern input, widescreen, high-refresh rendering, Lua mods, bots and experimental co-op.
lead_stories.why_it_matters: Readable, rebuildable game logic makes problems that emulators can only work around from outside directly fixable in source.

reader.standfirst: This is the reconstructed game itself compiled as a modern program, not an N64 emulator and not wholesale binary recompilation.
body: The upstream GoldenEye decompilation reached its matching milestone in August, producing source that can rebuild the expected ROMs.
Goldeneye-Native puts SDL/OpenGL or Metal underneath that source and can therefore change game-level behavior directly.

Its timing work is especially instructive: GoldenEye ties some simulation behavior to rendered frame iterations, so simply drawing faster can make the world run faster. The author documents failed measurements before separating world time from renderer speed.
August 28 commits include validating the beginner install guide against an actual ZIP download and removing hard-coded personal paths and bundle identifiers.
reader.context: The user must supply a legally dumped ROM; no commercial game data is bundled.
key_points: Matching decompilation creates a verifiable source reference.
A platform layer replaces console-specific graphics, input and storage.
Source access exposes timing bugs that external emulation may only mask.
reader.limitations: It is an unofficial active alpha and some additions intentionally depart from 1997 behavior.
reader.what_to_try: Read the README section on frame timing; it is a compact lesson in measurement design.

lead_stories.headline: WeatherPaper gets year-scale battery life mostly by being awake for only seconds
lead_stories.summary: WeatherPaper is an ESP32-C3 weather display around a 4.2-inch e-paper panel and custom PCB. The project reports roughly 0.0494 mAh per refresh cycle and a 500-plus-day target from a 1500 mAh battery using deep sleep, an 80 MHz CPU clock and very short Wi-Fi sessions.
lead_stories.why_it_matters: The useful mechanism is duty cycle: minimizing how long expensive subsystems are awake can matter more than making every active operation slightly cheaper.

reader.standfirst: E-paper helps, but the larger battery lesson is to wake, do the expensive work quickly, then disappear back into deep sleep.
body: The project wakes, connects, fetches weather data, redraws the panel and sleeps. The author reports about 4.3 seconds of active network time per cycle.
Optimizations include downclocking, static IP configuration and HTTP keep-alive. It also uses HTTP rather than HTTPS for public weather data to avoid TLS setup cost.
That last choice is a real tradeoff, not a universal recommendation: saving energy also gives up transport authenticity and confidentiality.
reader.context: The repo includes firmware, PCB Gerbers and enclosure files; Adafruit resurfaced the project on August 25.
key_points: Wake duration is a primary battery budget.
Network setup can dominate intermittent IoT energy use.
Power optimizations can trade away security properties.
reader.limitations: The 500-day figure is an estimate from measured per-cycle consumption, not a completed 500-day endurance test.
reader.what_to_try: Write a one-cycle energy budget for any always-on gadget idea before choosing hardware.

lead_stories.headline: Agent oversight research is finding that better traces can save time without making humans more accurate
lead_stories.summary: Human-computer interaction research found that ordinary agent action traces are cumbersome to verify. A redesigned oversight interface reduced time spent finding errors but did not meaningfully improve final verification accuracy; an August 24 position paper separately argues that agent use can erode the human skills oversight depends on.
lead_stories.why_it_matters: A human approval button is not meaningful oversight unless the evidence, timing and reviewer expertise support real judgement.

reader.standfirst: A giant trace can be technically transparent while still being operationally opaque.
body: Three user studies examined how people verify computer-using agents. Alternative presentation reduced review time, but higher confidence did not produce meaningfully better final accuracy.
A separate August 24 position paper argues that repeated dependence on agents may also weaken the skills required for supervision.
The practical implication is selective evidence plus drill-down: intended action, evidence, changed state, uncertainty and reversible checkpoints, with raw trace available when needed.
reader.context: The lead evidence comes from HCI user studies; the newer paper is a position paper rather than a controlled benchmark.
key_points: More trace detail is not automatically better oversight.
Review burden is a design variable.
reader.limitations: The studies cover specific tasks and interfaces and should not be generalized mechanically to every workflow.
reader.what_to_try: Replace a default full transcript with a compact evidence packet and preserve the raw trace behind it.

items.headline: AliceMemory makes corrections, provenance and review part of memory itself
items.summary: Alice stores decisions, open loops, resumption briefs and revisioned memories locally, with policy-checked writes and a review console. Its README explicitly separates a privileged benchmark path from the actual product retrieval path.
items.why_it_matters: Durable memory becomes governed state rather than an automatically trusted summary.
items.why_i_might_care: A wrong remembered decision can be more damaging than forgetting.
items.potential_connection: Study revision chains, proposal-versus-commit boundaries and source-backed recall for MAPS.
items.limitations: The published LongMemEval number uses a privileged store-chunk path; the product-path score is not yet published.

items.headline: Marky is a focused Markdown reader that live-reloads files agents are writing
items.summary: Marky opens files or folders, live-reloads changes and renders math, diagrams and highlighted code without becoming a full note-taking platform.
items.why_it_matters: It solves one mundane problem well: reading generated Markdown as it changes.
items.why_i_might_care: Useful for agent-written plans, docs and handoff files.
items.limitations: Latest commits I found are from April 2026.

items.headline: pano_z80 turns an obsolete thin client into a 25 MHz Z80 without soldering
items.summary: A Pano Logic thin client's FPGA is reprogrammed as a Z80 computer with RAM, USB keyboard/storage, VGA and a RISC-V I/O coprocessor.
items.why_it_matters: It reuses discarded hardware by replacing its logic-level identity.
items.why_i_might_care: It joins retrocomputing, firmware replacement and old hardware repurposing.
items.limitations: The main branch has seen no substantive work since 2020-2022.

items.headline: Useful now: weak-authority memory writes should be proposals, not facts
items.summary: Alice separates ordinary commits from review-required proposals and preserves correction history.
items.why_it_matters: Memory needs an authority model: who may assert, revise and supersede durable state?
items.potential_connection: Test MAPS states such as observed, proposed, reviewed and locked.

items.headline: Interesting research: optimize oversight for error detection, not trace completeness
items.summary: A redesigned oversight interface reduced review time but did not materially raise final accuracy.
items.why_it_matters: A shorter review is useful only if it preserves the evidence needed to catch consequential mistakes.

items.headline: Goldeneye-Native is already modifying systems that emulation leaves entangled
items.summary: The port separates renderer speed from frame-based world timing and exposes modern platform code plus Lua hooks.
items.why_it_matters: A decompilation becomes most valuable when it acts as an editable reference, not merely a completion percentage.

items.headline: Xodus shows Linux game compatibility moving into service archaeology
items.summary: Identity, entitlements, encrypted packaging and runtime services now matter alongside DirectX and CPU compatibility.
items.why_it_matters: Future preservation may need platform protocols as much as binaries.

items.headline: Marky: open a Markdown file and watch it update live
items.summary: A small desktop viewer with folders, live reload, Mermaid, math, syntax highlighting and fuzzy navigation.
items.why_it_matters: It is a narrow utility rather than another all-purpose knowledge system.

items.headline: look is a local-first cross-platform launcher with a Rust core
items.summary: look searches apps, files, folders and clipboard history from the keyboard and keeps its index local.
items.why_it_matters: It is an open-source command-palette workflow for Linux, macOS and Windows.
items.limitations: I did not independently benchmark its indexing speed or memory use.

items.headline: WeatherPaper treats wake time as the primary battery budget
items.summary: The project combines e-paper with deep sleep and aggressively short network activity, while publishing firmware, PCB Gerbers and enclosure files.
items.why_it_matters: It is a practical example of system-level low-power design.

items.headline: How a tiny device gets a year of battery life: duty cycle
items.summary: Average energy is current multiplied by time. WeatherPaper lets Wi-Fi be expensive for a few seconds, then spends almost all of its life in deep sleep; shortening setup by seconds can matter more than shaving milliamps from brief code.
items.why_it_matters: The same reasoning applies to sensors and ambient displays.

items.headline: Humans can review faster without reviewing better
items.summary: An agent-oversight interface reduced time spent finding errors but did not meaningfully raise final verification accuracy.
items.limitations: Interface and task effects may not transfer directly to coding-agent workflows.

items.headline: AI Agents Push Humans Out of the Loop
items.summary: An August 24 position paper argues that agent systems can weaken effective oversight structurally and by eroding the expertise required to supervise them.
items.limitations: This is an argument and synthesis paper, not a new causal estimate of skill atrophy.

items.headline: A thin client that forgot it was a thin client and became a Z80
items.summary: pano_z80 reloads the FPGA in a discarded Pano Logic appliance so it behaves as a 25 MHz Z80 machine with USB storage and VGA.
items.why_it_matters: It is closer to replacing a computer's identity than emulating one inside its original software stack.

sections.title: You Probably Didn't Know You Were Interested In This

items.headline: Archiving AI models may look more like preserving scientific instruments than saving software
items.summary: Project Pergamon is designing an archival process that includes weights, tokenizer, architecture, provenance and integrity metadata, with LTO tape and BagIt-style packaging as an initial substrate.
items.why_it_matters: A model file without its tokenizer, configuration and lineage may become as uninterpretable as an old binary without its platform.
items.potential_connection: This connects digital preservation, software archaeology and AI without requiring interest in model training itself.
items.limitations: Pergamon is an early initiative, not yet a proven long-term institution.

items.headline: Compatibility layers are becoming protocol archaeology
items.summary: Xodus illustrates a shift from reproducing CPUs and graphics APIs toward reconstructing identity, licensing, packaging and service contracts.
items.why_it_matters: Cloud-era software preservation may require preserving server-side contracts as carefully as executables.

items.headline: Review-governed durable memory
items.summary: Alice distinguishes immediate commits from review-required proposals and keeps provenance and correction history attached to durable state.
items.potential_connection: Study explicit authority states and supersession chains rather than flat latest-truth files.

items.headline: Risk-shaped oversight views
items.summary: Oversight studies suggest that showing every action is burdensome, while a faster interface still may not improve correctness. The mechanism is selective evidence plus drill-down, not less evidence overall.
items.potential_connection: Test review packets containing intent, evidence, changed state, uncertainty and reversible actions, with raw trace on demand.

items.headline: Service boundaries as compatibility contracts
items.summary: Xodus is converging on a service process that mediates clients, Xbox services and game-facing runtime calls.
items.potential_connection: A systems example of keeping volatile external integrations behind a stable internal boundary.

rabbit_hole.headline: Read Goldeneye-Native's failed frame-timing fixes before the final solution
rabbit_hole.summary: The README explains why comparing state at a fixed rendered frame produced reassuring but wrong results, then shows the real-time measurement that exposed the simulation-speed bug.
